sentences.text: A few special cases to finish, and each one is a favorite exam question.
An air-cushion vessel, when she’s operating in the non-displacement mode, adds an all-round flashing yellow light.
A wing-in-ground craft, when taking off, landing or flying near the surface, adds a high-intensity all-round flashing red light.
Under the International rules, a power-driven vessel under seven meters, whose top speed is no more than seven knots, may show just an all-round white light, and sidelights too if practicable.
On a boat under twelve meters, the masthead light or all-round white light doesn’t have to be exactly on the centerline, if that isn’t practicable.
And one for the Inland rules.
On the Great Lakes, a power-driven vessel may carry an all-round white light in place of the second masthead light and the sternlight.
Lights from sunset to sunrise and in restricted visibility.
Masthead two twenty-five, sidelights one twelve and a half, sternlight one thirty-five.
And for ranges, think six and three, five and two, two and one.
Next time: the lights of vessels that are towing.
